cat > .github/workflows/triage.yml <<'EOF'
---
name: triage

# pull_request_target runs in the context of the base repository, so the token
# can write to pull requests opened from forks. This is only safe because the
# workflow never checks out or executes code from the pull request.
on:
  pull_request_target:
    types: [opened]

permissions: {}

jobs:
  triage:
    name: Triage
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      pull-requests: write
      issues: write
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
      GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
      PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
      # Untrusted values are passed through the environment, never interpolated
      # into the script.
      PR_AUTHOR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.user.login }}
      PR_TITLE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}
    steps:
      - name: Post welcome comment
        run: |
          printf 'Welcome, @%s! Thanks for opening a pull request: **%s**.\n\nA maintainer will triage it soon.\n' \
            "$PR_AUTHOR" "$PR_TITLE" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/comment.md"
          gh pr comment "$PR_NUMBER" --body-file "$RUNNER_TEMP/comment.md"

      - name: Apply needs-triage label
        run: |
          gh label create needs-triage --description "Awaiting triage" 2>/dev/null || true
          gh pr edit "$PR_NUMBER" --add-label needs-triage
EOF
cat >> README.md <<'EOF'

## Triage workflow

`.github/workflows/triage.yml` runs when a pull request is opened. It posts a
comment that welcomes the contributor by username and repeats the pull request
title, and it applies the `needs-triage` label (creating it if missing).

It uses the `pull_request_target` trigger so the token can write to pull
requests opened from forks; the plain `pull_request` trigger gives forks a
read-only token. This is safe only because the workflow never checks out or
runs code from the pull request, and it passes the title and username through
environment variables rather than interpolating them into scripts. Keep it that
way: do not add a checkout of the pull request head to this workflow.
EOF

content.text:
I added `.github/workflows/triage.yml` and a "Triage workflow" section in the README. I haven't run it, because it only triggers on a real pull request.

**What it does:** when a pull request is opened, it comments "Welcome, @username! Thanks for opening a pull request: **title**" and applies the `needs-triage` label. It creates the label first if the repo doesn't have it.

**Forks:** the workflow uses the `pull_request_target` trigger. A plain `pull_request` trigger gives fork PRs a read-only token, so the comment and label would fail. Because that trigger runs with write access, the workflow never checks out or runs the PR's code. The PR title and username go in through environment variables instead of being written into the script, so a hostile title can't inject commands. Its permissions are limited to `pull-requests: write` and `issues: write`.

**Implementation:** it uses the `gh` CLI that comes with the runner rather than a third-party action, so there is nothing extra to pin. The README explains why `pull_request_target` is used and warns against adding a checkout of the PR head to this workflow.

I haven't committed anything.
